items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: But with Sam Taylor and Red Prysock and these guys, they were playing blues changes

ctx.x: Yeah, the chicken sound. But that was more or less original with him, wasn't it?

Yeah, that was original. That was him, and he did that on "Charlie Brown." He played that sound. But with Sam Taylor and Red Prysock and these guys, they were playing blues changes, I mean and the basic, not the modern blues changes, but the basic blues changes -- that's what these guys were playing. And then King Curtis came later on with "Charlie Brown," with this chicken sound and it seemed like all the tenor players that couldn't play this type of horn like Sam Taylor and Red Prysock and then, latched on to…
Now this Red Prysock -- what was his name?
